extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, creative-writing students, instructors, and critics
extracted.subtask_description: A technique-by-technique inventory of fiction craft (beginning, point of view, stream of consciousness, etc.) used as a reference for writing, teaching, or analysing short and long fiction. Each entry exemplifies the technique with passages, definitions, history, examples, and guidance on when to use it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: How a story opens: choices about hook, tone, information, and initial perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how the opening establishes voice, stakes, and reader engagement; different techniques suit different kinds of story (no single 'right' approach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: How a story concludes: resolution, ambiguity, emotional payoff, and thematic closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the ending to the mode and aims of the work; endings can confirm, complicate, or subvert expectations depending on technique and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of View
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of narrative vantage (first, third, omniscient, limited, shifting) and its effects on knowledge, sympathy, and reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate consistency, appropriateness for the story's needs, and how POV shapes what is shown/hidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introducing a Character
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for first presenting characters: what details to reveal, when, and how to convey personality and role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use introduction to create immediacy and distinctiveness; consider showing vs telling, names, actions, and speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for generating tension and reader expectation about outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage information distribution, stakes, pacing, and uncertainty; suspense can arise from both plot and character dilemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and use of character and place names as a stylistic and symbolic resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names can suggest character, era, social background, or thematic resonance; choose names deliberately to support tone and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sense of the Past
rubrics_metrics.description: Ways fiction evokes history, memory, and temporal depth in characters and setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include backstory, analepsis/time-shift, and descriptive markers that situate narrative in historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephoning (in fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling telephone conversations and mediated communication as a narrative device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone scenes require attention to exposition, immediacy, and how off-stage interlocutors are represented; can create distance or intimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing a title and its relation to theme, tone, irony, or reader expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles can frame interpretation, serve symbolic function, or misdirect; treat the title as part of craft, not merely a label.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Sense of Place
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating vivid, credible settings that root action and character in specific locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sensory detail, spatial relationships, cultural markers, and integration of place with character psychology to build place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stream of Consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Rendering continuous flow of a character's thoughts and perceptions (examples: Joyce, Woolf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires techniques for interiority and syntax that mimic thought; useful for deep subjectivity but can challenge readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior Monologue
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct presentation of a character's inner speech or thoughts (Joyce is a primary exemplar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide between quoted inner speech and free indirect forms; consider rhythm, punctuation, and how much consciousness to expose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate repetition of words, phrases, or motifs (example: Hemingway).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repetition to create rhythm, emphasis, or thematic resonance; avoid inadvertent redundancy that weakens prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defamiliarisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Making the familiar seem strange to renew perception (Shklovsky concept; Tolstoy's 'Kholstomer' cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use altered perspective, unusual detail, or stylistic estrangement to refresh readers' apprehension of ordinary things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-Shift / Analepsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Shifts in narrative time such as flashbacks (Ford Madox Ford referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle temporal transitions clearly to avoid confusion; use shifts to reveal backstory, irony, or to reframe present events.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Intrusive Author
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorial commentary or presence within the narrative voice (examples: Fielding, George Eliot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider rhetorical effect: irony, moral commentary, framing; intrusive voice can guide interpretation but may distance reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Unreliable Narrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrators whose credibility is compromised (Booth, Ishiguro cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design clues to unreliability and manage reader inference; unreliability can create mystery, irony, or thematic complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Epistolary Novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative conveyed through letters, documents, or other first-person artifacts (Richardson, Walker).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit multiple perspectives, authenticity effects, and the limits of documentary form; watch for plausibility of letter-writing as plot device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Indirect Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Blending narrator and character voice to present thoughts and perceptions without quotation (Austen, Flaubert, James).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to achieve intimacy while retaining narrator's control; requires careful syntactic and tonal modulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing and Telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between dramatizing events (showing) and summarizing or explaining (telling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance both modes according to pace and emphasis: show for immediacy, tell for compression and commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different Voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of multiple distinct narrative voices or perspectives in a single work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each voice is differentiated in diction, viewpoint, and reliability; multiple voices can expand scope but risk fragmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coincidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of chance events to move plot or create irony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coincidence can be used sparingly for comic or fateful effect but overuse undermines plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of objects, actions, or details to stand for larger meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate symbols organically; avoid heavy-handedness that reduces subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: Extended metaphorical narrative where elements systematically correspond to ideas or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegory clarifies an argument or moral but can limit ambiguity; choose scope and explicitness according to aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancy between appearance and reality, expectation and outcome, or voice and situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irony can operate at multiple levels (verbal, dramatic, situational); calibrate for tone and thematic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metafiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction that self-consciously reflects on its own status as fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metafictional devices to question narrative authority or explore form, but be wary of alienating readers if purely self-indulgent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intertextuality
rubrics_metrics.description: References, echoes, or structural borrowings from other texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intertextuality can enrich meaning and create dialogue with tradition; ensure references serve the work rather than merely signal erudition.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Comic Novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelistic strategies and tone aimed primarily at comic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include irony, timing, characterization, and incongruity; balance humor with narrative stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrealism
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of dreamlike, illogical, or hallucinatory elements to disrupt realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surreal techniques can probe unconscious or symbolic truths; maintain internal logic or intentional incoherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magical Realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of fantastical elements into realistic settings in a matter-of-fact way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the miraculous as ordinary to reveal cultural or thematic layers; keep tone consistent to avoid parody.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Nonfiction Novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid form that uses novelistic techniques to tell factual narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to factual accuracy, ethical representation, and transparency about fictionalized elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique of suggesting rather than stating facts, motives, or meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on subtext, reserve, and reader inference to create depth; avoid vagueness that confuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas (novels of ideas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Works organized chiefly around intellectual argument or exploration of concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance intellectual content with character and narrative energy to prevent didacticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Experimental Novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Formally innovative novels that challenge conventions of plot, language, or structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess formal risks against coherence and reader engagement; experimentation should serve expressive aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lodge's Chapter Method for Technique Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each chapter: (1) quotes a passage exemplifying the technique, (2) defines the term, (3) traces its history briefly, (4) discusses examples, (5) suggests when/why a writer might use it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this five-step method as a template for learning, teaching, or evaluating techniques; pay attention to exemplar passages and historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique as One Option (No Single Right Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The view that each technique is 'one of many available — no single right approach.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works by fitness of technique to aims rather than adherence to prescriptive rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique Best-Fit Contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Each technique has best-fit contexts — consider when/why a writer might use a given technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge a technique by its appropriateness to genre, voice, theme, audience, and narrative aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Vocabulary Sharpens Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Using and knowing precise technical terms helps both readers and writers identify and discuss craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt shared vocabulary (e.g., 'free indirect style', 'analepsis') to make critique and revision more precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tradition as Toolbox, Not Constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary tradition provides a toolkit of techniques rather than immutable rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn historical exemplars to borrow, adapt, or subvert techniques while keeping creative freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testability of Technique Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Each category is framed as 'testable'—you can ask: 'Does this story use defamiliarization? Free indirect style? An intrusive narrator?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete textual evidence (passages, patterns, syntactic choices) to diagnose whether a technique is present.
